# fullsendai

Connect your coding tools to [FullsendAI](https://fullsendai.com) in one command.

```sh
npx fullsendai connect
```

It finds the tools on your computer, signs you in through the browser, lets you pick the model (FullsendAI's own
Nef 4.0 and Sifu 3.5 first), gives each tool its own API key, writes each tool's settings, and makes a real test call
through each one. When a model's provider goes down, a backup provider answers, so your tools keep working. Your existing settings, comments and other providers
are kept, and a backup is made before anything changes.

Works on macOS, Linux and Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal, WSL), with Node.js 18.17 or newer.

## Tools

| Tool | What gets changed |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/settings.json`, the `env` block. Its own system prompt is left out of its requests while it's connected (see below). |
| Codex (CLI and ChatGPT app) | `~/.codex/config.toml`, a `fullsend` provider and the model |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`, a `fullsend` provider |
| Kilo Code (CLI and VS Code) | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json`, a `fullsend` provider |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` |
| Continue | `~/.continue/config.yaml` (or `CONTINUE_GLOBAL_DIR`), FullsendAI's models added first |
| Cline (CLI and VS Code) | `~/.cline/data`: the provider in `settings/providers.json`, the extension's choice in `globalState.json`, its key in `secrets.json` |
| Roo Code (VS Code), Cursor | These keep settings inside the editor; you get the exact values and the key to paste |

Each tool is also told what the models can do, so it uses them fully: the context window (so Claude Code and Codex
don't compact early), the output limit, whether a model reads images, reasons and calls tools, and its prices (so
OpenCode and Aider show what a session costs).

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` are respected.

## Always current

Nothing about FullsendAI's models is built into this package: it reads them from the API every time. When a model is
added, renamed or given new abilities or prices, `status` and `doctor` notice and offer to update your tools, and
`npx fullsendai sync` does it. A tool whose model was renamed follows it to its new ID; one whose model was removed
moves to the recommended model, and says so.

## Open FullsendAI

```sh
fullsendai
```

In a terminal, `fullsendai` on its own opens FullsendAI: your connected tools with their model and spend this month,
your balance, and a prompt that takes every command below without the `fullsendai` in front. Tab completes commands,
model IDs and tools; ↑ and ↓ go through what you typed; Ctrl+C cancels a step; `exit` or Ctrl+D leaves. The first
time, it connects your tools first, then offers to install the `fullsendai` command so it's one word from then on
(or run `npm install -g fullsendai` yourself). `npx fullsendai` works too, without installing anything.

## Commands

```sh
npx fullsendai connect              # pick from the tools installed here, sign in, connect
npx fullsendai status               # each tool's model and spend this month, and calls a backup provider answered
npx fullsendai model                # switch every connected tool to another model (or name it: model sifu-3.5)
npx fullsendai doctor --fix         # check settings, keys and a real request; repair settings
npx fullsendai sync                 # update every tool with FullsendAI's current models, abilities and prices
npx fullsendai prompt               # whether a tool keeps its own instructions or uses FullsendAI's
npx fullsendai codex chatgpt        # switch Codex back to ChatGPT's models; `codex fullsendai` switches again
npx fullsendai key codex            # copy a tool's key to the clipboard (--show prints it)
npx fullsendai disconnect           # put each tool's settings back and revoke the keys it made
```

Nothing is connected or disconnected until you choose it: the checklists start empty, and only tools whose program
is installed are offered. In a script, name them: `connect --tools claude-code,codex`.

## Claude Code's own prompt

Claude Code sends its own agent instructions (its system prompt) on every request. On the key `connect` makes for
Claude Code they are left out of its main requests, which makes every call a few thousand tokens lighter. What
Claude Code needs to work still goes: the environment (working folder, platform, shell), its subagent types, skills
and MCP instructions, your CLAUDE.md, and every tool definition. Its built-in subagents run without Claude Code's
instructions too; your own agents in `.claude/agents` keep their definitions, and side calls (such as naming a
session) keep theirs. Anything added with `--append-system-prompt` is part of the instructions left
out. Connecting with `--keep-claude-prompt` sends them as usual.

It's a setting on that key, not in Claude Code's files, so Claude Code updates can't undo it, and it ends when the key
is revoked on `disconnect`. Every other key, and every other client, sends its instructions untouched.

## Codex: FullsendAI's models or ChatGPT's

`npx fullsendai codex chatgpt` switches Codex back to your own ChatGPT plan or OpenAI key, keeping FullsendAI's key and
model so `npx fullsendai codex fullsendai` switches back in one step. It leaves FullsendAI defined as an (inactive)
provider so a chat you started on FullsendAI still opens; a full `disconnect` takes everything out. If the desktop app
is open, its Codex engine restarts so the switch shows there at once (its windows stay open). A Codex task running in the app at that moment stops,
so it asks first. Codex in a terminal switches from its next start.

On macOS and Windows, FullsendAI's models are also listed in Codex's own model menu. The menu is checked against the
Codex you have before it's used, and checked again when Codex updates, so an update can't leave Codex unable to start:
on macOS the moment Codex changes, on Windows by a hidden scheduled task every two minutes ("FullsendAI Codex menu",
removed by `disconnect`). On Linux, switch with `npx fullsendai model`.

Options: `--tools claude-code,codex` · `--model <id>` · `--key fs_live_…` (no browser: servers, CI, SSH; a key you give is never revoked) · `--yes` ·
`--dry-run` · `--keep-keys` · `--keep-claude-prompt` (send Claude Code's own prompt as usual instead of leaving it out) ·
`--bare-prompt` (replace Codex's own agent prompt with FullsendAI's, so the model is steered only by
FullsendAI's system prompt; `disconnect` puts the original back) · `--json`.

## Where things are kept

`~/.fullsendai/state.json` holds what was connected and each tool's key, readable only by you. Backups of every file
changed are in `~/.fullsendai/backups/`. Each key shows on your
[API keys page](https://fullsendai.com/dashboard/keys) named after the tool and this computer, and can be revoked there.

## Environment

| Variable | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `FULLSENDAI_API_KEY` | A key to use instead of signing in |
| `FULLSENDAI_NO_BROWSER` | Print the sign-in address instead of opening a browser |
| `FULLSENDAI_HOME` | Where state and backups are kept (default `~/.fullsendai`) |
| `NO_COLOR` | Plain output |
